title: The Endurance Crew All Come Home
text:
In January 1915 Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance froze into the pack ice of the Weddell Sea, short of the Antarctic coast where he had meant to land and cross the continent on foot. For ten months the ice carried the ship north. Then it crushed her, and in November 1915 she sank. Twenty-eight men were left on drifting floes with three small boats and whatever they had dragged off the wreck.

Shackleton changed the goal from crossing Antarctica to bringing every man home. He kept routines going, shared the same rations as everyone, and put the men most likely to grumble in his own tent so their moods would not spread. When there were too few warm fur sleeping bags to go round, lots were drawn, and according to Alfred Lansing's account the draw was quietly arranged so that Shackleton and his senior men got the thinner woolen ones.

In April 1916 the floes broke up and the men rowed to Elephant Island, their first solid ground in well over a year. It was far from any shipping route, so Shackleton took five men in the lifeboat James Caird across some 800 miles of the Southern Ocean to South Georgia. He, Frank Worsley and Tom Crean then crossed the island's unmapped mountains on foot to reach the whaling station at Stromness.

On Elephant Island, Frank Wild kept the remaining twenty-two men fed, busy and hopeful through four months of waiting. After three failed attempts through the ice, Shackleton returned on the Chilean tug Yelcho on 30 August 1916. Every man of the Endurance party was alive.
lesson: In a long crisis, the team's spirit is a survival resource. Share the hardship visibly, keep routines, and keep difficult moods close where you can manage them.
people: Ernest Shackleton, Frank Wild, Frank Worsley, Tom Crean
location: Weddell Sea, Elephant Island and South Georgia, Antarctica
source: Ernest Shackleton, South (1919); Alfred Lansing, Endurance (1959)
caveat: The expedition's Ross Sea party on the other side of the continent lost three men; the 'all came home' record applies to the Endurance party.
